findings.place: Between a in A comma and card
findings.evidence: A live three-bar existential-looking sign is unmistakably present. Its middle/right return may be a small adjoining s; the crop does not distinguish that from the sign’s flourish. No cancellation stroke extends across this locus.

findings.place: Cancelled formula, point after final slash
findings.evidence: A small dark ink mark stands just below and right of the slash. It is not erased or dismissed, but its function as a full stop rather than an unfinished quotient mark remains uncertain.

findings.place: Part a heading: ens

findings.place: Part a: canceled function and interlinear seg
findings.evidence: The lower token remains crossed and its middle is ambiguous between réal and rel. The live seg is visibly above it, not a baseline continuation; the insertion state is retained.

findings.place: Part a: dummy index throughout the segment formula
findings.evidence: All three little indices have an arch with a descending right exit; no clean crossing stroke is visible. They look more like n than x, but a compressed cursive x remains possible. The recurring ambiguity is marked at its first occurrence only.

findings.place: Part b: word to the right of quotient slash
findings.evidence: The initial rel and later tall stroke/dotted region can be followed, but the very reduced middle does not warrant an unmarked full-word reading. No unequivocal superscript abbreviation can be isolated. The word stands above d’équiv., on two lines.

findings.place: Bracketed paragraph, immediately after opening bracket
findings.evidence: The large loop and distinct high dot favor Si. The following reduced stroke does not securely establish whether on is also present, and On is not completely excluded. The alternatives are reordered without supplying a grammatical completion.

findings.place: Attachment diagram at right of bracketed first line
findings.c: \partial X\to S;\ \cap;\ X, in a separate centered block
findings.final: Right-side diagram: \partial X\to S, with \cap beneath \partial X and X below it
findings.evidence: The lower half shows a detached cap-shaped inclusion sign, no vertical arrow shaft or arrowhead. The diagram is at the right end of the first bracketed line; that layout is retained rather than moving it to its own centered line.
findings.math_note: The cap-shaped sign expresses the pictured inclusion vertically; it has not been replaced by a conventional hook arrow.

findings.place: Second bracketed line, quoted attachment verb and preceding words
findings.evidence: The initial et on is visible, followed by paired high quotation ticks. Inside, a reduced a, two tall strokes and a final che-like group favor attache, while the faint joins keep the word doubtful. The ink does not show the longer recollement.

findings.place: Second bracketed line: sign/word between X and S
findings.evidence: The crop shows two detached marks, the lower one slightly larger and slanted. They look like a colon, but an accent over a highly reduced a cannot be excluded. C’s unmarked à is no longer secure.

findings.place: Second bracketed line: after S, before boundary-map formula
findings.evidence: A tall descending stroke and a detached/reduced horizontal group can be compressed par. If read as a sign, the horizontal part extends right from the upright, hence \vdash orientation rather than H’s dashv. Neither word nor sign is secure enough to leave unmarked.

findings.place: Interlinear word in final quoted title
findings.evidence: The enlarged crop shows a looped initial g, a detached accent, a small e and a low om group. There is no tall l to support plane and no separate terminal point after m. The insertion stroke points between Réalisation and rectiligne.

findings.place: Last paragraph: fini and its parentheses/points
findings.evidence: The crop shows f-i-n-i, without a final s, then two distinct low points. The opening parenthesis is immediately before fini, not before d’un graphe.

findings.place: Quotation marks around final Réalisation ... rectiligne
findings.evidence: The crop shows two high upright ticks at the opening and two oblique high ticks at the closing, not guillemets.

findings.place: Final line, real-field capital

notes: Independent reading restricted to the scan004 packet, the three named images, conventions, PREAMBLE, supplied prior notation snapshot, and the subsequently supplied H drawing supplement. Whole image and each half were each viewed once. Nineteen separate unresolved loci received one crop apiece; no crops were repeated.

The sheet defines graphs by two sets and an incidence relation, gives one numbered axiom, defines strict graphs and arcs, then begins topological and rectilinear realizations. The final sentence stops after homéom. dans.

One live underlined main title Graphes. The underlined Def/Graphe labels and Axiome are not promoted to editorial section headings. Réalisation topologique d’un graphe itself has no visible underline; H’s emphasis there is treated as editorial formatting, not added manuscript text.
No date or authorial manuscript page number is visible. Archive foliation 3 is represented only as a TeX comment. H’s editorial page marker is not a collation difference.
No explicit authorial doubt word or question mark occurs. Parenthetical fini.. and dim finie... are retained as written, without interpreting them as editorial instructions.

All seventeen C doubt loci were given dispositions. Def, Axiome, sommet after 2, Arc, géom, and fini are resolved. Other original doubt loci are retained, with altered alternatives/order where warranted. New doubts concern the dummy variable, relation, the X-to-S word/sign, and the following compressed par/sign.

The supplied H drawing was inspected as witness H. Its topology is substantially present; it was not counted as absent. The upper branching dot is missing in H, while its detached smudge was missing in C. All graph edges, both curved lenses, the isolated edge, the isolated point and the unlabeled corners are represented in TikZ.
S.json is empty, so there are no sweep statements to confirm or overturn.

No comparison with another reader or page, OCR, web, recognition library, PDF text layer, or published text was used. Exact alphabet and small-word decisions were made from ink rather than mathematical expectations.

checks.statement: For a two-element set a, the displayed coordinate condition defines a segment with the two canonical endpoints.
checks.reasoning: Writing a={p,q}, the conditions 0<=t_p,t_q<=1 and t_p+t_q=1 give (t_p,t_q)=(u,1-u) for 0<=u<=1. The two coordinates equal to 1 in turn give the endpoints.
checks.outcome: Consistent with seg(a) and the endpoint injection in the manuscript. This check does not distinguish the written dummy variable n from x and does not certify the rest of the construction.
